text:
maya: heads-up — CI on M1 fails when Homebrew prefix has a space (OneDrive path). after brew install the binary isn't in $PATH, postinstall seems to try a fixed symlink path and dies. anyone seen this?

sam: ugh that sounds familiar. postinstall scripts sometimes assume /opt/homebrew/bin. can you paste the install output?

maya: here's the snippet i saw:
```
==> Installing redwoodctl...
mkdir: cannot create directory '/Users/maya/OneDrive - Redwood/Library/Homebrew/bin': No such file or directory
Error: Failed to link: /opt/homebrew/bin/redwoodctl -> /Users/maya/.../redwoodctl
```

maya: also, while trying to local test, redwood login fails when i'm using kubectl port-forward to the local controller. redwoodctl login --headless spins and then device flow times out. feels like the port-forward latency makes the device code expire.

jenna: two things: installer should respect `brew --prefix`/HOMEBREW_PREFIX instead of hardcoding /opt/homebrew. i'll add a fallback detection. for the auth -> port-forward problem, device-flow timeout is ~2m by default, and local port-forward can be slow. can you try increasing retries or running the auth from a host that has direct connectivity? i'll file a ticket for adding a flag to extend device timeout.

sam: opened PR #3421 to update postinstall to compute prefix from `brew --prefix` and to handle paths with spaces. added a small test that simulates a space in prefix. nightly artifact uploaded: artifacts/nightly/redwoodctl-m1.tar.gz

maya: trying the nightly now, thanks. quick note: when running localserve and port-forward i saw one timeout then a successful retry. so retry behavior helps but we should make it less fragile. @jenna can you add a line in the onboarding doc about avoiding OneDrive-like prefixes or how to fix them?

jenna: will add a short troubleshooting bullet + example `ln -s` workaround. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: nightly build for PR #3421 uploaded to artifacts/nightly/redwoodctl-m1.tar.gz

maya: confirmed nightly install succeeded on M1 with space in path, localserve + port-forward auth still timed out once but succeeded on retry. closing my immediate blocker, opening follow-up for device-flow timeout and a better retry UX. thanks all :pray:
